symptom.actual: context_os_audit.ok=false and control_plane.isolated=false; the Director final Provider request system message serialized a complete capability_token containing factory_run_id, JobToken identity, stage, project, and mutation scope.
symptom.expected: Capability and execution-attempt authority remain in the control plane and tool gateway. The LLM data plane receives only prompt-safe execution/evidence projections.

root_cause.mechanism: ContextOverrideProcessor and the ContextOS audit owned separate control-plane key sets, so capability and execution-attempt keys drifted out of the prompt deny-set. After top-level filtering, mixed data/control structures such as CE blueprints, handoff decisions, and execution envelopes were stringified without recursive prompt-safe projection. Opaque objects, serialized strings, hostile builtin subclasses, non-string mapping keys, spelling variants, and unbounded recursive/wide structures created additional authority-leak or request-assembly DoS paths.
root_cause.general_impact: Any Director request carrying JobToken or TaskRuntime attempt authority can leak control-plane identifiers and scopes to the model, fail ContextOS isolation auditing, waste context, and confuse authority with model-visible instructions.

fix_contract.required: Use one canonical control-plane prompt taxonomy for ContextOS audit and context override filtering. Recursively copy and filter mixed data/control mappings before provider-request serialization while preserving prompt-safe references and leaving the original context_override untouched for ToolGateway/DEO.
forbidden: remove capability checks from ToolGateway or DEO
